Hey Ben,
Try removing the aes call as below. You will want to read up on the differences between mapping and setting colors in ggplot2, e.g., page 48 of Hadley's book, as it can be confusing when you are first getting started.

Best wishes,
Doug

p<- p + geom_polygon(x=x2, y = y2, fill="white")
p<- p + geom_polygon(x=x3, y = y3, fill="white")
p<- p + geom_polygon(x=x4, y = y4, fill="white")
p<- p + geom_polygon(x=x5, y = y5, fill="white")
p<- p + geom_polygon(x=x6, y = y6, fill="white")

Hi everyone,

I am a newbie with ggplot and just having a little fun. I like it, but one of the  things that I am noticing is that the colors often display differently than I expect. With my first project, I just let things go, but as I work with r and ggplot, I would really like to get better control over what I am doing.

In the example below, I am making a superman emblem (because my son is 5 and likes superman, and it gives me a chance to learn how things work). The problem is, the white space is coming up black, and I don't know why.

Any ideas?

Thanks


-- 
Sincerely,

Ben Ditkowsky, Ph. D.
MeasuredEffects.com

library("ggplot2")

x1<-c(-18,0,-7,-29,-36,-18,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA)

You have two problems here. One that 'aes' stands for aesthetic
mapping: that means it is used to map an aesthetic to a variable. In
your usage you don't want to map it to a variable, you just want to
set it to a fixed value, so you should set the fill outside of the
aes() call. The second problem is that R is case sensitive, and the
aesthetic is called 'fill', not "FILL".

Correcting both of these issues gives a serviceable superman logo:

p<-ggplot(datf, aes(x1,y1))
p<-p+geom_polygon(fill="Red")

p<- p + geom_polygon(x=x2, y = y2, fill="white")
p<- p + geom_polygon(x=x3, y = y3, fill="white")
p<- p + geom_polygon(x=x4, y = y4, fill="white")
p<- p + geom_polygon(x=x5, y = y5, fill="white")
p<- p + geom_polygon(x=x6, y = y6, fill="white")

p

Just for fun, here is another approach to this task that may help you
understand some of the features of ggplot2:

## create data for superman logo
## don't need to fill in NA's, data.frame will do this for us
dat <- list(
x1 = c(-18,0,-7,-29,-36,-18),
x2 = c(-18,-13,-17,-19,-23,-18),
x3 = c(-18,-13,-10,-11,-17,-24,-29,-25,-23,-20,-18),
x4 = c(-10,-7,-6,-2,-6,-6,-12,-12,-14,-22,-24,-25,-25,-24,-22,-10),
x5 = c(-11,-10,-11,-11),
x6 = c(-25,-28,-34,-30,-31,-30,-27,-25),
y1 = c(-23,-5,0,0,-5,-23),
y2 = c(-21,-16,-17,-17,-16,-21),
y3 = c(-14,-14,-13,-12,-11,-11,-10,-14,-13,-13,-14),
y4 = c(-7,-8,-9,-5,-2,-5,-5,-4,-2,-2,-3,-4,-5,-6,-7,-7),
y5 = c(-2,-1,-1,-2),
y6 = c(-1,-1,-5,-9,-7,-5,-2,-1)
)

## combine x and y values

datf<-data.frame(x1,x2,x3,x4,x5,x6,y1,y2,y3,y4,y5,y6)

## reshape to get all the x's and y's in one column each
library(reshape2)
datfm <- cbind(melt(datf[grep("x", names(datf))],
id.vars=NULL,
value.name="x",
variable.name="xvar"),
melt(datf[grep("y", names(datf))],
id.vars=NULL,
value.name="y",
variable.name="yvar")
)

## create a variable that separates the red and white areas
datfm$c <- ifelse(datfm$xvar == "x1", "r", "w")

## plot
ggplot(datfm, aes(x=x, y=y, group=xvar, fill=c)) +
geom_polygon() +
scale_fill_manual(values=c("red", "white"))


Best,
Ista
